review_notes: I read the whole target file and the declarations it depends on: ModDualityDatum and ModZigzagDatum in KeyLemma.lean, freeMod and regularMod in ModTensor.lean, tensorLeftMod in TwistShuffle.lean, and OddLine in Prop29.lean. I compared them with Mathlib's Monoidal/Mod.lean. That file has ModObj, Mod, Mod.Hom, Mod.regular, Mod.comap and Mod.forget. It has no free-module construction, no relative module tensor, no duality datum for modules and no odd-line notion, and I found no free-module or duality-datum counterpart elsewhere in Mathlib/CategoryTheory. The only competing concept I found is `regularMod` in ModTensor.lean. It is a reducible alias of Mathlib's `Mod.regular`, and its docstring says so. That is outside the target file, and the target file never uses it. The target's own declarations (unitFreeDatum, freeSelfDatum, lineDatum, twistDatum and the matching zigzag theorems) are specific compositions of this library's datum and transfer constructions. They are not independent versions of anything in Mathlib. I cannot rule out a conceptual overlap with Mathlib's ExactPairing or rigid-object API, but ModDualityDatum is a different, relative-tensor notion, so I did not report it.
